quest.title: Secret of the Scorching Desert
quest.description: As agreed, you go to the place designated by Rahman to exchange hostages...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1000, Primogem x30, Mora x40250, Memory of Flourishing Green x1, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

chapter.title: King Deshret and the Three Magi

talks.objective: Gather at the entrance to the village

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're all here so early!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Looks like we have everyone here. ...Isak, are you sure you want to come with us?

dialogues.speaker: Isak
dialogues.text: I'll watch from a safe distance. Dehya... I wanna be there to bring Grandpa home.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Okay. Let's go then.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Dehya, wait.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: What's the matter?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: I heard that you were quite reckless yesterday... No more of that today, understood? Or I'll be very upset with you.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: *sigh* Fine.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Heh, they got here before us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh-oh, is it because Paimon overslept by five minutes and held everyone up?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You didn't have to admit to that.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Is everything ready?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Absolutely. Although...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: ...You brought fewer people than I imagined.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Bring him over.

dialogues.speaker: Isak
dialogues.text: Grandpa!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why is there only one of them?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Rahman, I've always thought of you as a man of his word. What's this about?

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: It's a one-for-one exchange. Sounds fair, don't ya think?

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Or lemme put it this way... Agreeing to any kind of deal with the Dendro Archon's people is already a huge compromise on my part. Don't you think you've asked enough?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: ...Uh-uh, you stay right there!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh... Paimon's dizzy...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Mmph...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is everyone okay!?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Ugh, this day's going just great...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Hmph, what a nuisance.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: The sand dune collapsed.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I saw an energy field... The Village Keeper protected us.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: It glowed green with Dendro. Just like you said, it may well have been the remains of Lesser Lord Kusanali's power inside the scholar's body.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No doubt.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You finally believe me.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...The Dendro Archon... The present one.

dialogues.speaker: Isak
dialogues.text: Grandpa? Grandpa? Oh no, he's getting confused again...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Hey, look around you.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Did there use to be a... temple here?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: It seems that when the sand dune collapsed, it exposed these underground structures.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The symbols on the gate belong to King Deshret's civilization. This structure must be ancient... Over time, the sandstorms completely buried it, and left it in the state we see now.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: ...It could have been an underground palace in the distant past.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Ohhh... A miracle! Praise King Deshret!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's he doing here!? And his men, too?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: They must have fallen down here with us. Pretty lucky if you ask me.

dialogues.speaker: Eremite Mercenary
dialogues.text: Ugh... Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Most of them seem in really bad shape, except for him. He got off lightly.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: ...Hmph.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Mind your head.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: No no, this isn't the time for conflict... Our exalted lord has shown us the way to his sacred palace.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He's not actually gonna go in there, is he...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: As it happens, I want to take a look inside, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What are you doing!?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Don't you think it's curious? One minute, Lesser Lord Kusanali's power protects us from harm, and the next... remnants of King Deshret's civilization appear.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Two major deities are vying to showcase their power to us. It would be a shame not to witness them both.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thought you weren't interested in gods!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Indeed. In my view, gods are just a higher form of living being... or "creature," you could say.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: New discoveries are always worth investigating. Whether they have anything to do with gods is neither here nor there.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Rahman, what are you gonna do about your men?

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: I'll just let them lay here — King Deshret will take care of his people... Right now, I'm going inside.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: It's full of life here.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: This defies comprehension... It looked completely desolate from the outside, yet it flows with energy inside.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, and there's so many plants. It's so pretty.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Sir Rahman.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: ...Huh? Me?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Do you see another Rahman here?

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Are you mocking me? What do you mean, "Sir"?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Interpret it however you want, but there's something I'd like to draw your attention to. While this structure is clearly left over from King Deshret's civilization, the energy that flows in here is that of the Dendro Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Whatever you say. It's not like I have a Vision.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: There's nothing to be angry about. Think of this as an academic journey.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: It does seem kinda strange. If that's true, then... we might have to explore this whole area to find an explanation.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Wait.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: What's that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A load of flowers... And it looks like there's something among them...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It looks like a tomb.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: These are King Deshret runes...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: They left something behind... Yes, it's an elegy written in an ancient script.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: What does it say?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: "Here lies our faithful priest, Kasala."

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: "His wisdom is a miracle among the people, deserving of high praise and admiration."

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: You can read ancient King Deshret script?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Of course. Every student needs to master at least 20 languages before they graduate.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He's not serious, right?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: There's still something off about this place... The elemental energy here is too concentrated.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: The scent of life... Is it trying to tell us something?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Hm...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Is this it?

dialogues.speaker: System Sound
dialogues.text: Analyzing...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: There seems to be a hidden message among these skeletal remains.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Excellent. There's a device from King Deshret's civilization in this gravesite. I'll transmit the information over and project it for everyone to see.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Isn't sharing knowledge against the Akademiya's rules?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Yes. However, under the circumstances, I'd prefer you to see this for yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: You'll understand after watching it.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: What was that...?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The priest's memories.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: No... no! Impossible!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata... So the former Dendro Archon and King Deshret were never enemies at all...

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: But... this doesn't make any sense! The Dendro Archon's followers... they're clearly...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Was that the former Dendro Archon? She became so tiny in the end...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Greater Lord Rukkhadevata came to the rescue of King Deshret and his people, but eradicating the forbidden knowledge took so much of her power...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The two deities' followers have resented each other all this time, completely unaware that their gods stuck by each other through life and death.)

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: You might be distrustful of the Akasha, but there's no reason for you to doubt King Deshret's technology.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: You've just witnessed his priest's last words.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: I've... never heard about any of this before...

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: The surviving followers of King Deshret all gathered in Aaru Village. Our god did not make mistakes... We refused to believe any of the rumors.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: King Deshret's death, the all-but-total annihilation of our civilization... It was all Greater Lord Rukkhadevata's doing!

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: We saw her as nothing more than a traitor, who stabbed us in the back in our moment of crisis... Just like us humans, fighting, feuding, double-crossing each other to survive in the desert.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: You were blinded by your prejudice.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Hah... haha... If I hadn't seen this for myself... If I hadn't witnessed his last words with my own eyes, ears, and heart...

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: How could I ever begin to accept this? The truth is so far from what I've always known. Am I really supposed to believe that after all these years... All this time seeking revenge... Suddenly now my enemy is my savior!?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Rahman... That's enough.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Give it a rest. You're starting to make a fool of yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: ...Dehya, tell me...

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: My Eremites and I... What are we even fighting for?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Rahman takes some time to collect his thoughts, while the rest of the party continues to explore the temple.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Rahman's reaction is nothing strange. To any believer, the truth he had just witnessed would have been difficult to accept.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hey, how're you doing?

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: ...I'll live, heh. Thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: I should probably go. I can't just stay here forever.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: What's your next move gonna be?

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: I know what you're going to ask... I feel deeply ashamed of everything I've done. You'll get everything you're asking for.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: But please, give me some time. After everything that's happened here today... Somehow, I need to explain it to the others.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: It's not gonna be easy.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Well, I guess that's for me to deal with. Dehya, this is where our camp's located. Make a note of it.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: When would be a good time for us to go?

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Tomorrow. I'll convince everyone that we're all on the same side.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: And I'll return every last one of your mad— Sorry, your Village Keepers. We'll share our other resources with you, too.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: You seem to finally understand that our true enemy is the sages.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Yes. The gods never gave up on anyone. It's the people responsible for all this that need to face the consequences of their actions.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That must've been rough, but he seems to have figured things out now.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: *sigh* Rahman's no fool. Being the leader of your own faction in the desert is no easy feat.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: It's too bad he was held back by his belief in King Deshret, but now that that's changed, I guess we have a few more people on our side.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This is a turn for the better.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The outcome, at least, is favorable.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We should get going too. Let's head back, have a proper meal, and a nice, long sleep! We'll need all our energy tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cynooooo! We're leaving!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...Stop yelling.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Rahman, we're here.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Everything's been arranged. Someone will bring the Village Keepers back to Aaru Village shortly.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I guess all I can say now is... thanks for agreeing to help.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Don't mention it. I think we can both agree you went to hell and back for it.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: But we share a common cause now. From here on out, we're allies.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Where are the perpetrators?

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: I'll bring you to them. Follow me.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: So these are the people who kidnapped the Village Keepers.

dialogues.speaker: Morghi
dialogues.text: Oh no, it's the scribe!?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: There's no need to yell. No one can help you now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've been all over the desert trying to find you!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: That's right.

dialogues.speaker: Morghi
dialogues.text: General Mahamatra!? No, no! M—Make it quick, please! Swift and painless...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, the moment they set eyes on Cyno, they turn pale like they've seen a ghost...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: You should've known that I would be coming for you.

dialogues.speaker: Morghi
dialogues.text: W—Wait! We were just following orders! You know what I'm talking about, right? Th—There's no way we could've done all this by ourselves!

dialogues.speaker: Judar
dialogues.text: No, not Cyno... He's gonna tear us limb from limb!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I could do worse.

dialogues.speaker: Morghi
dialogues.text: P—Please have mercy!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Start talking. Otherwise, I'll have to resort to... other methods.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: So... Your superiors have kept you quite busy recently. Why? What are they trying to accomplish?

dialogues.speaker: Judar
dialogues.text: Um... they, um, wanted to extract Canned Knowledge...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Don't play dumb. You know what I'm really asking.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: They extract Divine Canned Knowledge... then what?

dialogues.speaker: Morghi
dialogues.text: I... I, uh, really don't know how to explain it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, you better start talking, or you'll be sorry!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: You don't wanna make things any more difficult for yourself, do ya?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: May I ask them a question?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Be my guest.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The sages are trying to create a new god, aren't they?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Huh? That sure didn't sound like a fancy metaphor or anything... You're serious, aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Morghi
dialogues.text: How did you know?

dialogues.speaker: Judar
dialogues.text: There's no use hiding it now... Yes, you're right.

dialogues.speaker: Judar
dialogues.text: The Akademiya is working on an important and potentially world-changing project. They are creating a new god... a god that will belong to them, and to the people of Sumeru.

dialogues.speaker: Judar
dialogues.text: It may seem as if Sumeru's academics are thriving, but ever since the death of Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, scholarly breakthroughs have been few and far between.

dialogues.speaker: Judar
dialogues.text: The withering of Irminsul has been getting worse recently. The sages have tried everything they could think of, but nothing's worked. I'm always hearing them say things like, "If only Greater Lord Rukkhadevata was still with us..."

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...Continue.

dialogues.speaker: Judar
dialogues.text: And then, someone from the Fatui showed up. They called him "The Doctor"... He brought a... a "Gnosis," and said he wanted to borrow the Akademiya's research facilities.

dialogues.speaker: Judar
dialogues.text: The Doctor was previously expelled from the Akademiya. At first, the sages looked down at him in disdain... But when he said those words, everyone's expression changed.

dialogues.speaker: Judar
dialogues.text: He asked them: "Do you wish to create a god?"

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: ...This is what the arrogant ignorance at the extreme end of academia looks like.

dialogues.speaker: Judar
dialogues.text: First, the Akademiya spent a long time constructing a "divine vessel," which was based on an exquisite humanoid puppet.

dialogues.speaker: Judar
dialogues.text: After that, they harvested dreams via the Sabzeruz Festival samsara, maximizing the Akasha's output...

dialogues.speaker: Judar
dialogues.text: With The Doctor's help, and the Akasha now functioning at maximum efficiency, they were able to use it to extract the power from the Gnosis and convert it into a "divine core."

dialogues.speaker: Judar
dialogues.text: Next, they decided that their new god needed to possess "divine wisdom." For that to happen... they needed a huge quantity of Divine Canned Knowledge.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: ...It adds up.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: But how do you determine whether the knowledge extracted is of divine origin?

dialogues.speaker: Morghi
dialogues.text: Call it an educated guess... The Akademiya has been trying to figure out the exact source of the scholars' madness for centuries, but to no avail...

dialogues.speaker: Morghi
dialogues.text: Nobody can explain the cause of this phenomenon. Surely you can see what that implies, Scribe Alhaitham?

dialogues.speaker: Morghi
dialogues.text: If it's knowledge no mortal can comprehend, then it must be something only gods are able to decipher. In other words... it's the source of the God of Wisdom's omniscience and omnipotence.

choices.text: But the sages' end product won't be Greater Lord Rukkhadevata...

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: You must have noticed by now — the Akademiya doesn't care about who their god is. It's the ability to exercise control over knowledge and wisdom that matters.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: It is as if they are cursed with a desire for omniscience and omnipotence that burns in their blood.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Some organisms demonstrate phototaxis, and thus orient their entire lives in respect to sources of light. For the sages, their only source of hope is the existence of a deity who embodies the acme of wisdom.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: This is but a form of phototaxis. For many scholars, the absence of a God of Wisdom means stumbling in the darkness for the duration of their lives.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Then what does Lesser Lord Kusanali mean to you?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Is she not a true god present in this world? If you already have a new god, why try to create another one?

response.speaker: Morghi
response.text: ...From the beginning, the Akademiya has never treated her as a god.

response.speaker: Morghi
response.text: When the Akademiya first discovered Lesser Lord Kusanali, the newborn God of Wisdom, the sages hoped that she would be as wise as Greater Lord Rukkhadevata. But upon evaluation...

response.speaker: Morghi
response.text: They found that, at that time, she possessed no more intelligence than any ordinary human child. The sages never had a ruder awakening... This forced them to accept that Greater Lord Rukkhadevata had indeed passed away.

response.speaker: Morghi
response.text: Not to mention that Lesser Lord Kusanali's Gnosis has been used to power the Akasha this entire time. By herself, she has neither an archon's raw power, nor the spectacular insight expected of a God of Wisdom...

response.speaker: Morghi
response.text: Slowly but surely, people began to forget about her existence.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: So... this is the path the sages have chosen?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Even now, they still refuse to acknowledge Lesser Lord Kusanali...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (...I never imagined a god could be subjected to such cruelty.)

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Alright, let's try to keep our cool. If everyone's in a bad mood, then let's change up our scenery.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Rahman, give me a few men to help us escort the Village Keepers back to the village. And these two scholars — they're coming too.

response.speaker: Rahman
response.text: Sure, as you wish.

talks.objective: Go back to the village chief's house

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: The Village Keepers you found have all been returned to their homes, and each one has a dedicated caregiver to look after them. The two new scholars are being kept under close supervision, too. Really great work, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... the atmosphere's so heavy...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (It's hard to not feel weighed down by what we just learned.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Despite everything Lesser Lord Kusanali has done for her people, the Akademiya has abandoned her in the Sanctuary of Surasthana like a lost cause...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Even those she's protected have never realized there's such a small and childlike god in the world.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, say something! Stop spacing out!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: C'mon, is there... nothing left to talk about? In that case, let's all get some water and try to think about something else.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Or, I can go fetch some snacks...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon's so coming with you!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Do you have any plans, Traveler?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Gods above, you're not talking about work, are you...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I want to share everything I know with all of you.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Hm, so you were still witholding some information?

choices.text: Yes, I'm sorry. I had my reasons...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: In between the conversations, Candace and Paimon bring over snacks and tea.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Dehya's expression is relaxed, as if her mood hasn't been affected by the heavy conversation at all.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Cyno has a firm and solemn expression on his face. It looks like he's made up his mind about something.\nThe core of his beliefs, his motivation to pursue the right course of action... everything is now clear to him.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The core of his beliefs, his motivation to pursue the right course of action... everything is now clear to him.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Alhaitham also turns towards the crowd. He wants to listen, too.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: ...After that, the whole story comes out.\nAll the experiences, feelings, and secrets are shared freely with everyone.\nTo share everything means to consider everyone as allies. From today on, everyone will fight for the same goal.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: All the experiences, feelings, and secrets are shared freely with everyone.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: To share everything means to consider everyone as allies. From today on, everyone will fight for the same goal.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even though we lived through all of this firsthand, it still feels super surreal to hear you talk about it again.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...That's everything we've experienced so far in Sumeru.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: What a whirlwind of a story! I felt like I was holding my breath the whole time.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: ...It seems like there will be more issues to face in the days ahead than I had anticipated.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Still, now's a good time to make our next move. Now that Rahman's joined us, we'll be an even stronger team.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: It's time to make a plan.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Indeed. These events are a flagrant transgression of the rules in every sense. We cannot allow it to continue.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: So, everyone, are we on the same page?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Crush the sages, and rescue our god... that is our ultimate goal.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Well, let's brainstorm a little more about what other resources we can draw on.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: The next time we gather here, we must have a solid plan.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep! It'll work out for sure!

choices.text: But now I know we're all in this together.

dialogues.speaker: Ceremonial Guide
dialogues.text: Look up at the hall as a mortal and listen to King Deshret's holy guidance.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Message
dialogues.text: After six days infiltrating the temple, I finally understand the priests' parlor tricks.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Message
dialogues.text: <color=#00E1FFFF>The elevator will descend to the ground. Get on top of it before it starts ascending again to reach the dome.</color>

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Message
dialogues.text: Nonsense like "Forbidden ground ahead, mortals shall not pass" or whatever are just made up by the priests to hoodwink us.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Message
dialogues.text: I leave this method here in hopes that the people of King Deshret who shall travel here in the future shall freely enjoy the privilege of witnessing his sacred presence.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's getting brighter! Ooh, it looks so beautiful!
